Sri.Chethan B., counsel for the appellant, Sri.Manjunatha Rayappa., Additional Government Advocate for respondents 1 and 2, appeared in person and Sri.Prashanth B.R., counsel for respondent No.3, appeared through video conferencing.

2. The captioned appeal is filed to modify and enhance the awarded compensation in the judgment and award dated 09.10.2015, passed by the Court of the II Additional Senior Civil Judge and JMFC at Hassan in L.A.C.No.53/2015 on several grounds as set out in the memorandum of appeal.

entities.text: II Additional Senior Civil Judge and JMFC at Hassan
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: NC: 2026:KHC:6510 HC-KAR 3.
Counsel for the respective parties presented several contentions.

Sri.Chethan B., counsel for the appellant in presenting his arguments, strenuously urged that the issue involved in the present appeal is squarely covered by the order made by the Division Bench in MFA No.10457/2018, along with connected matters, which was disposed of on the fifth day of February, 2025.
Sri.Prashanth.B.R., and AGA submits that they support for the award made by the Reference Court.

Counsel for respondent No.3 submits that the Cauvery Neeravari Nigam Ltd. is the beneficiary of the acquisition, and it was not arrayed as a party to the proceedings before the Reference Court, and only in this appeal it has been impleaded.
Hence, he submits that the matter requires a remand to enable them to adduce evidence.
It has been vehemently contended that the claimants must establish the market value by evidence, and they cannot NC: 2026:KHC:6510 HC-KAR rely on the judgments / orders of this Court.
Accordingly, he prayed for the dismissal of the appeal.

sentences.text:
4. Heard the arguments and perused the papers and the citations with care.
5.
Has the award passed by the Reference Court been just and proper?
NC: 2026:KHC:6510 HC-KAR 6.

It suffices to note that the appellant was the absolute owner of the land bearing Sy.No.314/3 measuring 03 Guntas and Sy.No.255/1 measuring 06 Guntas situated at Doranahoshalli Village,
Kasaba Hobli, Hassan Taluk and District.
The said lands and other adjoining lands were acquired under a preliminary notification dated 06.05.2010 and a final notification dated 01.08.2011.
On a re-appreciation of the evidence and material on record, the Division Bench has modified the award and enhanced the compensation to Rs.1 lakh.
As the Division Bench has already rejected respondent 3's request for a remand, the same is declined in the present appeal as well.

Since the subject land and the land involved in the decision referred to supra are similarly situated, possess the same potential value, and were acquired for a common purpose, the principle of parity must apply.
Denying the same enhanced compensation amounts to unjust discrimination, violative of Article 14 of the Constitution.
NC: 2026:KHC:6510 HC-KAR

Adhering to the doctrine of parity, the appellant is entitled to the same benefits as allowed in [MFA NO.10457/2018 c/w MFA NO.10456/2018] because the land is contiguous, acquired for the same purpose, and the discrimination against these landowners is unsupported by law.
7.
For the foregoing reasons, the appeal is allowed.
The market value of the lands bearing Sy.No.314/3 measuring 03 Guntas and Sy.No.255/1 measuring 06 Guntas situated at Doranahoshalli Village, Kasaba Hobli, Hassan Taluk and District is re

- determined at Rs.1,00,000/-
per Gunta with interest and statutory benefits.
The claimant is not entitled to the interest for the delayed period of 1159 days.
